# Closing check of M0-e-04: the hardening round S3 (lane `check/M0-e-04-close-s3`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-19)

Lane `check/M0-e-04-close-s3` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code in a Claude Code cloud container (Linux x64, Node
24.12.0). `tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib` at both
sittings. The first sitting ran from 01:45 to about 03:10 (UTC). The container then restarted and cut short that
sitting's RELATED run. The second sitting ran from 06:25 to 08:40 under the CONTINUE RULE. It kept the first sitting's
mirrors, logs and probe outputs, which survived in the session scratchpad, and re-ran the gates, RELATED and NEAR. A
third sitting (from 11:25, CONTINUE RULE) read NEAR's finished log, re-ran `landed:verify`, re-confirmed that the tree
equals the `after` mirror, ran H6d over the census probe, and wrote this verdict and the records. The seat is an
implementer-side, independent checker. It is not the round's author (`build/M0-e-04-fix-s3`, L-0560). It closes the
session's hardening round S3 (J237 (2), J186, J192) on the sixteen FIX-NOW rows of `checks/hardening-inventory.md`
§M0-e-04. It is not the re-check of a failed check. The checker's ledger row is **L-0561**.

The seat ran no git command. It changed no file of the item. It planned its 35 mutants and its probes (CHECKPOINT
01:52) before it read the author's 'Hardening round S3' section. It ran one vitest process at a time
(`tools/test_budget.py` printed 1). It read the before-image from `main`'s objects with its own read-only Python
reader of `.git/objects` (`objread.py`, no git command). Twelve files differ from that image: the round's five sources
(`src/districts/{faces,grow,perimeter,stage,table}.ts`) and seven test files (`test/districts/{grow.test,
integration.test,land.test,perimeter.test,stage.test,support,typing.test}.ts`). The landed record equals the tree on
all 29 paths. The mirrors are under the session scratchpad's `waves/check-M0-e-04/s3/`:

* `after` is a copy of `plat/` without `node_modules`, the tree as landed. In the second sitting, `diff -rq` of
  `packages/layout/src` against the tree printed nothing, and `cmp` was equal on all 12 changed files.
* `bef` is the same tree with `main`'s five sources put back. It runs the round's tests on the pre-round code.
* `mut` holds the mutants. Each source was restored after its mutant, and `diff -r` against `after` was then empty.

Each mirror was installed from the lockfile (`--frozen-lockfile`). No symbolic link in any of them resolves into the tree,
and `@plat/kernel` resolves inside the mirror. The mirrors' `node_modules` were removed after use.

## Verdict: PASS. All sixteen rows are confirmed, and no blocker was found

Labels: **CONFIRMED** means executed by this seat, and **PLAUSIBLE** means reasoned. The mutants ran one at a time in
`mut` as `vitest run --maxWorkers=1 <the row's test file> -t '<the row's pin>'`, so each kill is credited to the row's
own pin. The two survivors ran on their whole files, without `-t`. The cross run ran the round's six test files on
`bef`. It printed `Test Files 4 failed | 2 passed (6)`, `Tests 7 failed | 80 passed (87)`.

**Behaviour: the declared shift is confirmed exactly.** This seat's census probe (`zz-census.test.ts`, 192 lines per
image) covers S6 on towns 1 – 100, on `land:0` towns 1 – 6, on CITY 1, 2 and 4, and on growth 1 and 2. It also
covers `settlementPerimeter` on the flat fixture's outlines 1 – 40 at 50 m and 180 m. Its result
(`census-before.txt` `88105da3…`, `census-after.txt` `abdb0578…`):

* 12 lines differ, on towns 12 21 26 38 55 66 81 84 86 89 92 98.
* On each of them, only `mergesSeq` and the `grown` face-append order move.
* `districts`, `seams`, `quarters`, `typing`, `report`, `per`, `hint`, `lin`, `owner` and `mergesSet` are identical.

This is C-0375's declared shift, town for town. No golden or digest records `grow`'s order, so none needed
re-recording. CONFIRMED.

Class: the outline is LAWFUL, and `refusal-census.md` R-06 classes the union's chains as OUR OWN INTERMEDIATE. Either

and the census's round table routes R-04 – R-06 to M0-a-05. So Q64 is rightly not merged here. No lawful class is left
at REFUSE by this item's code. The six seeds stay with the session's router round (note 11, Q64, R-06). CONFIRMED.

## New findings (the blocker rule)

No new finding is a blocker. There is no gate red. No interface or test id the item lists is missing. There is no
unstaged stub, and no wrong result on an honest input. There is no clean-room breach and no path outside `plat/`.
Three notes are appended to `checks/M0-e-04-notes.md` (N-s3c-1 – N-s3c-3).

**JUDGMENT (vetoable): the survivors T4e and H6d are hardening rows, not blockers.** The brief says that a
non-equivalent survivor on a stated promise stays a blocker. This seat reads that clause as covering the promises the
round's failing lines state, as `checks/M0-a-06-s4.md` read it. Both survivors are live, and both mark a missing pin
on code this seat's probe confirms correct:

* **T4e.** Row 4's source note and its inventory row name two readers that ignored the run's tables, `typingCells`
  and `minBarrierClass`. Both are threaded and pinned (T4a – T4d killed). `rosterBuildings` is a third reader, which
  the round threaded by its own choice (C-0375 (3)). The probe shows that it is threaded correctly. On town 4, an `s6`
  with `roster` `buildings.CITY` = 100 handed in through `withS6` moves N_q from 13 to 5 and changes the quarters.
  Under T4e, N_q stays 13. No honest run reaches it, because no registry view carries `s6`.
* **H6d.** Row 6's promise is that no merge encloses a hole, and H6d keeps it. It only gives up the fall-through to
  the next neighbour. On the probe's 3 × 4 grid, S then stays below the floor and is reported, which is a typed,
  fail-safe outcome (N-45: a rare-case quality shortfall that fails safely). The round's code takes the next
  neighbour, as C-0375 (5) says: S merges into the bottom row, and every district keeps one boundary loop. The third
  sitting ran H6d over this seat's whole census probe (mirror `mut`, W=1, 366 s): `census-h6d.txt` is byte-identical
  to `census-after.txt` (sha256 `abdb0578…` both, 192 lines). H6d therefore moves no committed output on any
  registered family (towns 1 – 100, `land:0` towns 1 – 6, CITY 1, 2 and 4, growth 1 and 2). Unlike
  `checks/M0-b-03-s5.md`'s C06, which changed a registered seed's output, it is reached only by the hand-made
  fixture. CONFIRMED.

If the session reads the survivor rule as binding here, each one needs one test, and the probe is that test (notes
N-s3c-1 and N-s3c-2).

**N-s3c-3 (for the session).** A variant `s6` now changes S6's output without changing the view's `hash`. This is row
4's REPORTED hash half. No honest run reaches it. It goes to the tables' owner and to a future composer, which must
thread one view through `siteFeatures` and S6.
